text:
jamie: Heads-up — we've got a persistent p95 spike on dedicated-pool-eu-west after last night's rotor failover. latency spikes for small-chat workloads, GPU util still ~55% but tail tokens/sec drops.

omar: Can you paste the graphs? p95 numbers?

jamie: p50=30ms, p95=1.2s, p99~2.8s for route `text.generate.small-chat` across pool-A. Token throughput down ~18%.

maria: Any obvious hot shards or rack hotspots? NIC errors?

jamie: No NIC errors. Telemetry shows uneven allocation: pool-A has 72% of live workers and pool-B sitting at 14%. Something in the rotor scheduling favored A after the inter-region failover.

ryan: That's the rotor balancing heuristic kicking in during failover — it prefers lower-latency AZs and doesn't account for recent warm-pool heat. We should manually nudge capacity to even out the hotkeys.

tayler: Could we redirect low-priority/queued requests to preemptible lanes (or hosted API) briefly? That'd reduce tail for dedicated customers but costs bn fallback.

jamie: I ran `curl -s https://internal-api/pools/eu-west1/status | jq .` and got: { "pool-A": {"workers": 86}, "pool-B": {"workers": 17}, "warm_pool": {"workers": 12} }.

omar: Oof. Why is warm_pool so small? Was scale-up disabled? Any recent autoscaler errors?

jamie: Autoscaler errored on `scale_up` at 03:08 UTC, stack trace snippet: ```Error: insufficient quota for gpu-v100, attempt=1/3
 at autoscale/provision.go:124
``` We retried but quota hit stuck some slots in pending.

maria: If we force-rotate 20% of traffic from pool-A -> pool-B that should flatten p95. What's the command for the rotor tool?

ryan: `tools/pool-rotor shift --from pool-A --to pool-B --percent 20 --dry-run` to preview. Dry run will output exact allocs. If safe, `--commit`. Watch egress and KV cache cold misses.

jamie: Dry-run gives: will move 18 workers and shift ~12% of active traffic. KV-cache miss rate expected to spike ~8% for those tenants.

tayler: Cost check — if we add more workers to warm_pool (= buy capacity) to hide the imbalance, estimated incremental cost ~ $4.8k/day for 48 GPUs. If we just rotate, cost ~ $0 but risk short-lived increases in latency for migrated tenants.

omar: We should prefer rotation + temporary preemptible fallback for non-critical tenants. Lower cost and reversible. What's rollback plan?

maria: Rollback = run `tools/pool-rotor revert --tag <run-id>` which reverses allocations in ~30s. Also `autoscaler resume` once quota clears. Monitor `route:p95`, `kv:miss_rate`, `gpu:util` and paging-alerts channel.

jamie: I'll run dry-run now and post results. @maria want to own commit if dry-run looks safe? @omar can you keep an eye on quota ticket with cloud? :eyes:

sre-bot: [ALERT] dedicated-pool-eu-west1 p95 latency > 1s (3m rolling). Incident ID: INC-2026-0423-euw-rotor

maria: happy to. If dry-run matches the expected 18-worker delta, I'll commit at +5m. We'll do preemptible redirect for non-prod routes first.

ryan: Also add a short-lived routing rule: `route.weight.adjust text.generate.small-chat non-prod: 0.15 -> preemptible` for 10m. That should shave the tail.

jamie: Dry-run output attached (inline): "to_move": 18, "expected_p95_improved": 0.45s, "kv_miss_increase": 8%. Looks reasonable.

maria: committing in 2m. Will annotate run-id and post monitoring snapshots.

omar: I've pinged cloud support for quota. If they unlock, we can scale warm_pool next week rather than buy long term.

tayler: Sounds good. Post-mortem note: rotor should include warm_pool weight in balancing heuristic. Filing a ticket: infra#2347.

jamie: +1. Thanks team — will post update when commit done. :thumbsup:
